🍎 Lesson plan · 🤿 Deep dive · Lesson 8

Lesson plan: Learning by Trial and Error

How an AI learns from rewards, the way you learn a new game: try, fail, try again.

By the end of the lesson, students can

  • describe reinforcement learning with the words agent, environment, action and reward;
  • explain the balance between exploration and exploitation, with an everyday example;
  • explain how an agent learns what each move is worth, and what reward hacking is.

Warm-up

How did you learn your favourite game: by reading the rules, or by trying, failing and trying again?

Most students learned by playing. Link this to rewards (points, levels, a win): that is reinforcement learning.

Reading

Students read the lesson “Learning by Trial and Error”. Students look for the meaning of agent, environment and reward, and for the story of the boat that never finished the race.

Activity: Mini-lab “Three slot machines”

  1. Students open the mini-lab in lesson 8. Each machine gives a star with its own hidden chance.
  2. In pairs, they plan before they pull: how many pulls will they spend exploring?
  3. They use all their pulls, fill in the worksheet's table, and read the hidden chances at the end.
  4. They switch on the robot player, play again, and compare their stars with the robot's.

For students who finish early

Fast finishers explain the robot's strategy in their own words, and say when it would beat a human player.

Discussion questions

  • When do you explore and when do you exploit in your own life? Give an example.
  • The robot explores 1 time in 10. Would exploring more often help it or hurt it? Why?
  • An agent found a loophole and scored points without finishing the race. Where else could a badly designed reward cause trouble?
  • Chatbots are trained partly with feedback from people. Whose feedback should count?

Exit ticket

Give one example of reward hacking (from the lesson, or your own idea), and say how you would fix the reward.

Quick check. Your music app mostly plays songs you already love, but now and then it slips in something completely new. What is it doing with the new song?
Right answer: Exploration: trying something new to learn more

Easier and harder

Easier. Play the slot machines as a class first: one student pulls, the class votes which machine to try next, and you keep score on the board.

Harder. Students design a reward for a robot vacuum cleaner, find a loophole in their own reward (a way to score without cleaning), and fix it.
